newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: COLSTON STILL HAS TIME TO RESIGN
The Senate President says Independent senator Mal Colston still has time to resign voluntarily from his position as Deputy President of the Senate.
The Senator's travel expenses are the subject of a federal police investigation.
But Margaret Reid says with less than an hour before the Senate sits, she's still not heard a word him.
She says Senator Colston doesn't have to resign the post in person, and could do it by fax or by dropping in a letter.
BEAZLEY DEMANDS COLSTON LEAVE PARLIAMENT
Federal Opposition Leader, Kim Beazley, says he doesn't want to see Senator Mal Colston around Parliament because he doesn't belong there.
Senator Colston is expected to quit as the Senate's Deputy President before Parliament resumes this afternoon, ahead of a formal move to to dump him from the post.
The Prime Minister has challenged the ALP to follow the Government's lead in not accepting Senator Coslton's vote, a tactic Labor Senator Robert Ray describes as a smarmy trick.
Mr Beazley says there's only one thing he wants Senator Colston to do, and that's resign immediately from the Senate, as he should have nine months ago.
HOWARD SAYS GOVT WON'T TOLERATE INTERNAL ATTACKS
The Prime Minister, John Howard, says the Government will no longer tolerate attacks from within Coalition ranks.
He wouldn't be drawn on who he was referring to ..but says criticisms have been about the pace of change, and calls for action on taxation including the introduction of a consumption tax.
Mr Howard has told ABC Radio the Government has allowed unreasonable criticisms to go unanswered.
LIBERAL MP CALLS FOR ALL TO IGNORE HANSON
Federal Liberal MP Chris Gallus says the media created a monster in Pauline Hanson, and continued attacks on the independent will only further her cause.
The member for Hindmarsh says recent attacks on the maverick MP are firming her position, not weakening it.
Ms Gallus says John Howard's initial approach of ignoring Pauline Hanson was the most sensible, and is one everybody should be taking.
MINISTER CALLS FOR CONVICTED KOREANS TO BE DEPORTED
New South Wales Police Minister, Paul Whelan, wants four Korean nationals jailed last week for burglary to be deported.
Mr Whelan is seeking an urgent meeting with the Federal Immigration Minister, Phillip Ruddock, about also tightening up tourist visa applications.
This follows the disclosure that the four men, who entered Australia on tourist visas, have criminal records in Korea.
Mr Whelan says he'll be raising the issue with state and territory Police Ministers at their conference next month.
He says there should be an appeal against the 18-month sentence imposed on four.
CLAIMS OF 800-MLN DLR CUT TO PHARMACEUTICAL BENEFITS
There are claims the Federal Government is planning to cut a further 800-million dollars from the pharmaceutical benefits scheme in next week's budget.
South Australian Labor leader, Mike Rann says the cuts are outlined in a leaked government document.
Mr Rann says the cuts target older Australians, who also lost out in last year's budget when the Government made consumers pay another 50 cents for subsidised prescriptions.
He says the Government has betrayed aged pensioners by singling them out for some of the worst budget cuts.
HARRADINE SPEAKS OUT ON MEDIA OWNERSHIP RULES
The man who could have the last say on the Government's proposed changes to media ownership laws says he belives diversity of ownership is very important.
As Federal Cabinet prepares to finalise its media law reforms, Independent Senator Brian Harradine says he'll consider the Democrats' call for a Senate Inquiry into the issue.
The reforms are expected to see the scrapping of rules preventing television station owners also controllling newspapers in the same market.
Senator Harradine says he's currently examining the issue, but would like to see diversity in media ownership maintained.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
